headlines.headline: St. Johns homeless day center scheduled to close Oct. 1
headlines.summary: The Do Good Multnomah-run homeless day center at 9000 N Lombard St in North Portland's St. Johns neighborhood is scheduled to close Oct. 1, 2026, ordered through a Multnomah County budget amendment sponsored by District 2 Commissioner Shannon Singleton after neighborhood complaints about trash, loitering, and camping around the small 800-sq-ft facility. A better, larger replacement location with real showers, storage, and space is planned, but no new site has been announced yet.
headlines.tell_wayne: The St. Johns day center in North Portland is scheduled to close today. If anyone you help used that spot for daytime services, they'll need somewhere else to go — no replacement location is open yet.

headlines.headline: City of Portland's winter 2026/27 plan: 580 regular overnight beds vs 876 last year; first-come first-served
headlines.source: Daily Tidings (citing City of Portland Shelter Services)
headlines.summary: The city's winter plan lists 580 regular adult beds (SE Grand Recovery 140, Burnside SAFES 100, Moore Street 100, Central Church of the Nazarene 100 including its fall expansion, CityTeam Grand 80, St. Stephens Church 60) plus 718 flex beds vs 867 last winter; shelters are first-come first-served, and SE Grand Recovery and CityTeam Grand expect sobriety.

headlines.headline: Bybee Lakes Hope Center raised $1.3 million to keep 100 threatened beds open
headlines.summary: After Multnomah County told Bybee Lakes it would lose 25% of its beds (100 beds) to budget cuts, founder Alan Evans says fundraising since January 2026 brought in $1.3 million, keeping the beds open temporarily; the center is considering operating independently of county funds.

headlines.headline: New: Good Circumstance, a women's day center and non-lending library in Old Town
headlines.summary: Good Circumstance opened a day space in Portland's Old Town for women and gender-expansive people: free computers and internet, community classes, walk-in peer support, and a warm place to rest — open Monday-Friday 8am-4pm; one block from SAFES.

headlines.headline: Rockwood Bridge Shelter in Gresham stays open under new management — Transition Projects takes over after operator dissolved
headlines.summary: The 42-bed transitional shelter on NE 181st Ave in Gresham's Rockwood neighborhood is still serving residents after its former operator Sunstone Way dissolved this summer; Transition Projects introduced its new team to the neighborhood Sept 17. Entry is by referral for adults already approved for permanent housing.

headlines.headline: Two Portland city councilors demand answers on Urban Alchemy shelter-staff misconduct allegations; $90M contract at risk
headlines.summary: After a KATU investigation found 80+ Ombudsman complaints about staff at Urban Alchemy (sexual harassment, drug use/dealing, theft, retaliation; five employees arrested in the past year) — Portland's largest shelter provider, running ~700 of the city's alternative shelter beds — councilors Candace Avalos and Sameer Kanal asked the city administrator for a full accounting by Monday, Sept 28, ahead of budget decisions that could pull the contract. No closure or access change yet. Independently verified by parent agent via KATU's own channels 2026-09-24.

headlines.headline: Cascadia Health opened Mountain View, a 10-bed secure residential treatment facility in Southeast Portland
headlines.source: Archynewsy (reporting Oregon Health Authority announcement; First Lady Aimee Kotek Wilson spoke at Sept 3 opening)
headlines.summary: Opened September 4, 2026 (slightly outside window, but new capacity), this 10-bed facility serves adults with serious mental illness plus co-occurring substance use, part of OHA's plan to add 1,660 residential treatment beds statewide.

headlines.headline: Multnomah County approves room-block deal for 50-unit Northeast Family Shelter at 4911 NE 82nd Ave
headlines.source: Citizen Portal (Multnomah County Board meeting summary), corroborated by Multnomah County Homeless Services Dept
headlines.summary: County board approved using a 52-room motel in the Cully/Sumner area as a family shelter run by Just Compassion, expanding county family shelter capacity from 84 to 106 units (over 25% more), with 28 families already in line to transfer — a real new shelter option for families with children.

headlines.headline: Portland's Largest Overnight Homeless Shelter Is Gone After Just One Year
headlines.summary: The 200-bed NW Northrup Shelter closed September 18; the city expects 580 regular adult overnight beds this winter versus 876 last year — fewer beds, so call shelters early.

headlines.headline: Changes for City Shelter Services
headlines.summary: Confirms the NW Northrup Shelter closed September 18, 2026; the Church of the Nazarene shelter stays open by private donation with 50 beds in summer and 100 in fall.

headlines.headline: Portland's only residential treatment center for women with children to close
headlines.summary: The Letty Owings Center, the only residential shelter for mothers in recovery, closes October 31 after 37 years — it is still open until then.

headlines.headline: Two New Affordable Housing Projects Move Forward with Portland Housing Bureau Support
headlines.summary: 82 affordable homes for low-income older adults (the fastest-growing homeless group) plus 24 for-purchase townhomes are now funded; these become housing options to ask case workers about as they move forward.

headlines.headline: 2026 mayoral candidates: 'Gresham is on the rise'
headlines.summary: Gresham mayoral and council candidates lay out their homelessness plans; the direction the east-metro city takes affects outreach, shelter, and encampment enforcement there.

headlines.headline: Two arrested in drug bust at city-run homeless shelter in Portland, police say
headlines.summary: Portland police made two arrests after a monthslong drug-dealing investigation linked to a North Portland Safe Rest Village; guests there should expect added security and know shelters remain drug-free zones.

headlines.headline: Changes for City Shelter Services
headlines.summary: Weidler Village and River District Navigation Center are closed and Reedway closed this month; pods move to a bigger North Portland Road site, but total 24/7 capacity drops from 867 to 718 people, so call ahead for bed availability; the county will now lead severe-weather activations using city shelter sites.

headlines.headline: Portland report maps complex journeys through homelessness ('Without a Map' study)
headlines.summary: PSU's final Pathways study found 98% of unhoused Multnomah County residents want permanent housing and showed missing IDs, caseworker turnover, and unreturned calls are common blockers — knowing these barriers helps people prepare paperwork and persist with outreach teams.

headlines.headline: Shelter leader fears people will be left on Portland streets as Northrup Shelter closes
headlines.summary: The NW Northrup overnight shelter is closing this month and neighboring Bethanie's Room already sees rising demand, so anyone using Northrup should line up another bed now.

headlines.headline: Blanchet House opens Bethanie's Room in NW Portland with 75 overnight beds for women
headlines.summary: A new 75-bed overnight shelter for women opened in Northwest Portland; women seeking nightly shelter have a new option to contact.

headlines.headline: Portland shelter raises $1.3 million to keep 100 beds open
headlines.summary: Bybee Lakes Hope Center raised $1.3 million from the community to keep 100 beds open after Multnomah County cut its funding, so those beds remain available instead of closing.

headlines.headline: Homeless Shelters That Work, Cheap-Ass Apartment Buildings, and Empty Senior Housing
headlines.summary: A KGW study found motel rooms and village-style shelters move people into permanent housing best; anyone choosing between shelter options should ask about motel placements or pod villages first.

headlines.headline: Year-over-year homelessness declines, but not in Oregon
headlines.summary: Oregon's homelessness rose 19% from 2024 to 2025 (over 23,000 people) while the national count fell, which is why state lawmakers keep emergency housing orders in place and funding pressure high.

headlines.headline: Wilson budget sends more homeless to N. Portland Road Safe Rest Village
headlines.summary: The North Portland Road Safe Rest Village is growing into the city's largest pod shelter (about 275 spots) as two other villages close; people placed there should know it is far from downtown services and plan transit accordingly.

headlines.headline: Year-Round Shelter Opens In Hillsboro
headlines.summary: Hillsboro's first year-round shelter offers 75 sleeping spaces (35 indoor beds, 40 pods), meals, hygiene and laundry, 24/7 staff, and allows pets — the main westside option for people in Washington County.

headlines.headline: Portland's Largest Overnight Homeless Shelter Is Gone After Just One Year
headlines.summary: Confirms the 200-bed NW Northrup overnight shelter in the Pearl District closed for good with its last guests on Friday, Sept 18, 2026, and no replacement 200-bed site is opening — overnight bed seekers must now look to other city overnight shelters (call 3-1-1).

headlines.headline: City update: NW Northrup shelter closed Sept 18; Central Church of the Nazarene stays open (50 beds, 100 this fall)
headlines.summary: The city's official shelter page was updated this week: NW Northrup Shelter is listed as closed (September 18, 2026), Central Church of the Nazarene stays open (50 beds summer, expanding to 100 in fall), and the city expects about 580 regular adult overnight emergency shelter beds this winter versus 876 the previous year.

headlines.headline: Multnomah County HSD September newsletter: new Homeless Services director, data-reform coverage
headlines.source: Multnomah County Homeless Services Dept. (HSD Monthly)
headlines.summary: Notes new HSD Director Nathaniel VerGow, an OPB 'Think Out Loud' interview on budget-constrained service delivery, and coverage of provider accountability — signals where county homelessness policy is heading.

headlines.headline: Oregon advances 66-home intensive supportive housing project in Clackamas County (Gant Gardens)
headlines.source: Oregon Housing and Community Services / Oregon Health Authority (via EIN Presswire)
headlines.summary: Gant Gardens is the first project under the state's new intensive permanent supportive housing effort pairing deeply affordable homes with around-the-clock behavioral health support — future housing for people with chronic homelessness and acute needs.

headlines.headline: State housing committee hears Oregon homelessness response results: 6,286 shelter beds added, 5,539 people rehoused
headlines.source: House Interim Committee on Housing and Homelessness (press coverage)
headlines.summary: Since January 2023: 6,286 new or maintained shelter beds statewide, 5,539 people rehoused, and 25,942 households kept from becoming homeless — context on what state programs are actually delivering.

headlines.headline: Northrup Shelter closure shifts demand to Bethanie's Room, now turning away 5-10 nightly
headlines.summary: Blanchet House's 75-bed women's shelter in NW Portland is at capacity and turning away 5 to 10 women each night since the city closed the Northrup overnight shelter; women seeking shelter should arrive early or call 211 for other options.

headlines.headline: Mayor Keith Wilson on Moda Center, police abolishment fight, and homeless shelters
headlines.summary: Mayor Wilson's latest interview covers the state of Portland's shelter system and budget cuts in plain terms for anyone wondering what the city is planning next for overnight beds.

headlines.headline: Multnomah County waits for colder weather before opening warming shelters
headlines.summary: The county is not opening severe weather shelters yet because forecasts do not meet its thresholds, so no extra overnight warming sites are available in the metro this weekend; regular shelters and 211 remain the routes inside.

headlines.headline: 'Lines just get so much longer': Pearl District women's shelter overwhelmed after closure of Northrup Shelter
headlines.source: KOIN (via brightgram mirror of KOIN story)
headlines.summary: Bethanie's Room, a Blanchet House shelter for women and families in the Pearl District, says it is being overwhelmed by extra people seeking a bed one week after the only downtown overnight shelter closed.

headlines.headline: Portland women's shelter overwhelmed after nearby closure
headlines.summary: Bethanie's Room is turning away five to ten women every night since the nearby Northrup shelter closed, and only six city-run shelters remain open.

headlines.headline: Portland overnight shelter forced to turn people away after nearby NW Northrup shelter closes
headlines.summary: A Northwest Portland overnight shelter says it is already feeling the strain and having to turn people away since the nearby 200-bed Northrup shelter shut down.

headlines.headline: Multnomah County unanimously authorizes submission of HUD Continuum of Care application amid legal uncertainty
headlines.source: Citizen Portal (Multnomah County board session summary)
headlines.summary: The county voted to rush a federal funding application by the September 30 deadline because the grant that pays for most of the area's permanent homeless housing (about $38.6M annually) is in court and now only partly guaranteed.

headlines.headline: Multnomah County is tightening its homelessness count — active list drops from ~18,000 to ~14,500
headlines.summary: The county is removing people it can't reach from its records, so the official homeless count will soon look about 3,500 people smaller — but nobody got housed; the same people are still outside. Day of article not verified; URL shows 2026/09.

headlines.headline: Portland public drug-use ban awaiting state action; Bybee Lakes saved by county cash
headlines.summary: Bybee Lakes — the region's largest shelter, which had 100 beds threatened by county cuts — is now being kept open with county money on top of $1.3M in community fundraising; the push to ban public drug use on sidewalks is waiting on the state, so nothing changes on the street yet. Exact episode date not verified.

headlines.headline: Portland's Largest Overnight Shelter Closes as Nearby Site Turns Away Up to 10 People Each Night
headlines.summary: The city closed its 200-bed Northwest Northrup overnight shelter over budget cuts, and nearby women's shelter Bethanie's Room is now turning away up to 10 people a night.

headlines.headline: Portland's Largest Overnight Homeless Shelter Is Gone After Just One Year
headlines.summary: A detailed follow-up confirms the Northrup shelter's last guests left September 18 and no replacement 200-bed site is waiting.

headlines.headline: Portland women's shelter forced to turn people away amid increased demand
headlines.summary: KGW reports Bethanie's Room is turning away five to ten women each night, with staff tying the surge to the Northrup shelter closure, and notes only six city-run shelters remain open.

headlines.headline: Portland will have nearly 200 fewer emergency overnight shelter beds this winter
headlines.source: Daily Tidings (City of Portland Shelter Services data)
headlines.summary: The city's 2026/27 winter plan lists 580 regular overnight beds versus 876 last year, with flex beds covering up to 718 total; all shelters run first-come, first-served.

headlines.headline: Under new management, Rockwood Bridge Shelter provides a place to stay
headlines.summary: Transition Projects took over the 42-bed Rockwood Bridge Shelter in Gresham's Rockwood neighborhood after Sunstone Way dissolved; it stays open for residents moving toward permanent housing.

severe_weather.text: No severe weather shelters are open right now. They open only when it is 25°F or below, or snow/ice hits set levels. City winter 2026/27 plan (published Sept 27, 2026): 580 regular adult overnight beds across six sites — SE Grand Recovery (140), Burnside SAFES (100), Moore Street (100), Central Church of the Nazarene (100), CityTeam Grand (80), St. Stephens Church (60) — plus 718 flex beds as demand rises; all first-come, first-served. Year-round shelter beds are open — call 311 (7am–8pm) for city shelters, or 211 (Mon–Fri 8am–6pm).
